history.contentIn: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was a Harvard University scientific proposal to study how tiny amounts of aerosol particles behave in the stratosphere. A very small amount of material — on the order of 100 grams to less than 2 kilograms, typically calcium carbonate (a common mineral found in limestone and used in products such as toothpaste) — would be released into a small mixed volume roughly 1 km long and 100 meters in diameter. The gondola would then fly back through that plume to measure aerosol microphysics, chemistry, and light scattering. A 2021 platform test in Sweden, planned with the Swedish Space Corporation from Esrange, was a hardware test only: the SCoPEx Advisory Committee recommended suspending it pending societal engagement, and no particles were to be released. In March 2024 Harvard announced that Keutsch was no longer pursuing SCoPEx; the platform is expected to be repurposed for stratospheric research unrelated to solar geoengineering.
